To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nurses prefer to communicate with the other nurse who is closest to the patient.
the communication pattern between nurse-nurse, nurse-physician, nurse-patient and nurse-devices is complex.

(i) nurses prefer to call the nurse in charge, (ii) there is a lack of prioritization in the alarm system, (iii) nurses prefer to communicate with the patients by using the patient’s name, and (iv) nurses prefer to use a mobile phone to communicate with the other nurses and physicians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the communication patterns between the nurses and the devices, and between the patients and the devices.
the following questions: What is the communication pattern between nurse-nurse, and nurse-patient, in the case of a patient alarm?
how the communication pattern between the nurses and the other health care actors could be improved, in order to increase the efficiency in the communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nurses prefer to communicate with other nurses by phone, and that they prefer to communicate with patients by face-to-face.
the communication between nurses and other health care actors should be improved, and the CallMeSmart should be improved to support this.
there is no clear communication pattern between nurses and other actors in hospitals regarding alarms and tasks, and that the communication pattern is highly dependent on context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nurses are not using the alarm system to its full potential, but instead use it as a reminder to do a task.
we need to look at communication in the context of the hospital.
nurses are very busy people, and that they need to be able to prioritize their tasks and alarms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nurses prefer to communicate with other nurses and physicians in a face-to-face manner, and that the patient alarms are prioritized by urgency.
nurses are very much aware of the communication pathways and that they are able to identify which actors should be contacted in case of an alarm.
there is a need to improve the communication between nurses, patients and devices.
